blogs.title: Reasonable Observer Overload: How *Santos* Nails Fair Use to the Objective Standard
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Second Circuit's pivotal shift away from subjective creator intent in the 'purpose and character' of use factor. Drawing on *Andy Warhol* and *Hachette*, the author explores how Judge Lohier reinforces the 'reasonable observer' test, effectively rendering the user's subjective motive irrelevant to the transformative nature of a work like the Kimmel satire segments.

blogs.title: Killing the 'Good Faith' Guardrail: The End of *Harper & Row* as a Hard Constraint
blogs.description: This legal commentary examines the second-circuit's explicit retreat from the 'good faith and fair dealing' requirement where previously established in *Harper & Row*. The post discusses how *Santos v. Kimmel* signals a doctrinal change in 2025, separating the affirmative defense of fair use from the ethical quality of the user's conduct, even in scenarios involving deception or molds.

blogs.title: Cameo Contracts and Third-Party Beneficiaries: The Privity Wall
blogs.description: This post explores the contract law dimensions of digital platform liability. It details how the Dr. Lohier Digital Litigation Court dismissed state law claims based on strict limits of third-party beneficiary status in Terms of Service agreements. The author discusses the implications for content creators, who are often non-signatories to ToS agreements used to generate content.
